title: Trial-shuffle null FAILS under jittered shared-event confound with zero true LFP-SPK coupling
notes: Requested by Hamm (2026-08-27 pre-P4 review): test the trial-shuffle null (used in test_F, test_causal_validation.py) against a HARDER adversarial case than test_F's -- P (LFP proxy) and R (spike proxy) driven by the SAME per-trial event onset but with DIFFERENT response kernels (P: broad gaussian sigma=25ms centered ~150ms; R: narrow gaussian sigma=5ms centered ~220ms), and explicitly ZERO direct coupling term between P and R in the generative model (independent noise, no P->R or R->P dependency beyond the shared event onset). Code: omission/tests/test_adversarial_shared_event_null.py.
Two conditions tested, 60 trials x 400ms each, n_perm=200 permutations, 2026-08-27 run:

CONDITION 1 (no jitter, identical event phase every trial): p=0.1045, observed_peak=0.199 at lag=+67ms (close to the true 70ms kernel-center separation -- a pure timing artifact, not real coupling), null_peaks mean=0.195 sd=0.003. Null narrowly avoids flagging this as significant, but NOT because it is correctly modeling the confound -- with zero jitter, the deterministic template is bit-for-bit identical at the same within-trial phase regardless of which trial's noise realization occupies that slot, so permuting trial LABELS cannot change the concatenated signal's deterministic structure at all. The null's near-observed-magnitude peaks reflect an undestroyed confound, not a correctly-calibrated test -- this passes 'by luck of scale', not by design.

CONDITION 2 (jittered, per-trial onset SD=8ms, closer to a real paradigm's trial-to-trial timing variability): p=0.0050, observed_peak=0.192 at lag=+68ms, null_peaks mean=0.169 sd=0.004. STRONGLY SIGNIFICANT FALSE POSITIVE. Mechanism: each trial's per-trial jitter is applied IDENTICALLY to both P's and R's kernel centers within that trial (a shared per-trial cause), creating genuine trial-paired covariation between P and R that is destroyed by permuting trial labels (a randomly mismatched P/R pair no longer shares that trial's own jitter draw) -- so shuffling DOES reliably lower the null statistic relative to the correctly-paired observed statistic, giving a small, well-calibrated-looking p-value. The null is correctly detecting that a real, trial-specific statistical association exists between P and R -- it is NOT correctly attributing that association to genuine LFP->SPK directional coupling. The association is real; its DIRECTIONAL/CAUSAL interpretation would be wrong. This is a classic common-cause confound (shared trial-level event timing), not evidence the null is broken as a general-purpose statistical tool -- it is evidence the null is answering a different question ('is there a trial-linked association') than the one a directional-coupling claim needs answered ('is that association due to LFP causing/preceding spike activity specifically').

Direct implication for the omission paradigm: trial-to-trial timing variability (reaction time jitter, fixation/behavioral state drift, imperfect experimental timing) is present in real sessions. Any SPK-LFP directionality claim built ONLY on within-condition trial-shuffle nulls is vulnerable to exactly this false-positive mechanism whenever LFP and spiking share ANY common event-locked drive with per-trial timing jitter -- which the omission paradigm's stimulus sequence onsets provide by construction. A trial-shuffle null alone is NOT sufficient evidence of genuine directional coupling; it rules out only the specific alternative that the FULL joint (P,R) pattern is exchangeable across trials, not that a shared, jittered common cause explains the association.

issues.description: Ordinary within-condition trial-label permutation, as implemented in omission.jnwb_ext.nulls.trial_permutation and used per Hamm's own spec for the F confound test, produces a strongly significant false positive (p=0.005) for a synthetic case with an explicitly zero direct-coupling generative model, once realistic per-trial event-timing jitter is present.
issues.action: P4/Analysis-A-E must NOT rely on trial-shuffle nulls alone to certify SPK-LFP directionality against the omission paradigm's own event-locked structure. Requires a stronger control per Hamm's own suggestion: event-template removal/residual analysis (regress out or subtract the trial-averaged evoked response from both P and R before computing lagged_association, so only trial-to-trial RESIDUAL variability -- not the shared deterministic template -- contributes to the association) or matched conditional modeling. NOT implemented yet in this build -- flagged as a required P4 design element, not fixed here.

verification.status: CONFIRMED (2026-08-27) -- independent verifier re-ran both conditions across 10 additional RNG seeds (3,7,11,42,99,123,555,777,2024,31415; none overlapping this session's original seeds), independently re-derived the mechanism from the generation code (onset_jitter drawn once per trial, added to BOTH P's and R's kernel centers -- confirmed shared, not independently drawn -- with separate/independent noise draws, confirming zero direct P<->R coupling term exists in the generative model), and independently audited lagged_association/trial_permutation usage for leakage or off-by-one errors (none found; usage matches test_F's convention exactly).
verification.key_result: Jittered condition: p=0.0050 in 10/10 independent seeds -- every run hit the permutation-test resolution floor 1/(n_perm+1), meaning the observed statistic exceeded ALL 200 null draws every single time. False-positive rate at alpha=0.05: 10/10 = 100% across independent seeds -- a saturating, deterministic failure mode, not a borderline or seed-dependent result. No-jitter condition: significant in only 1/10 independent seeds (p<0.05), confirming the original receipt's framing that its near-miss non-significance was 'by luck of scale' rather than principled confound control -- most seeds of the no-jitter condition don't even luck into a non-significant result.
verification.alternative_explanations_ruled_out: verifier confirmed p=0.0050 is exactly 1/(n_perm+1) (the permutation floor, not a display artifact), confirmed no leakage between the observed and null computation arms (R_shuffled freshly redrawn each of 200 permutations from the same R_trials pool), and confirmed a minor adjacent-trial concatenation-boundary bleed in lagged_association (pre-existing, not introduced by this test) applies identically to both the observed and null computations and therefore cannot explain the asymmetric result.
